references.text: Jacob had a meeting with God at Bethel, where God appeared to him in a dream, and Jacob promised to serve God there and build a house for Him.
Esau threatened to kill Jacob, and Rebekah sent Jacob away—the flight from Esau that God refers to in 35:1.
God identifies Himself as 'the God of Bethel' and tells Jacob to return to his homeland, which prepares the command in 35:1.
Abram built an altar for the Lord who had appeared to him, a parallel to Jacob's command to build an altar at Bethel.
God appears to Isaac, and Isaac builds an altar, paralleling Jacob's experience of God's revelation and altar-building.
Jacob fulfills God's command from 35:1 by building an altar at Bethel and naming the place El-Bethel.
Highlights the connection between God's command to go to Bethel (35:1) and the final naming of the place after meeting with God.
Provides the direct historical context (Rebekah's rescue of Jacob) for the flight from Esau mentioned in 35:1.
